ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory customer due diligence under CMF art. L.561-4-1 to L.561-10: (i) identification and verification of the legal person's existence and of each UBO holding more than 25% of capital or voting rights; (ii) systematic PEP status determination for all directors and UBOs; (iii) screening against the consolidated EU financial sanctions lists (Regulation (EU) 269/2014, Regulation (EU) 2580/2001 and all implementing Council Regulations), the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the French asset-freeze file (Fichier des comptes gelés of the Direction générale du Trésor) and OFAC's SDN list (recommended as mandatory by French clearing banks for Swift-TT and Revolving-LC payment rails routed through USD); (iv) monitoring under TRACFIN reporting thresholds (CMF arts. L.561-15 and R.561-12) and (v) enhanced due diligence where the foreign shareholder's domicile appears on the FATF or French 'Lutte contre le blanchiment' high-risk lists.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique électronique des formalités d'entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) – https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; company-name and trademark conflict search on the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RNCS) database and INPI trademark database at https://data.inpi.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name (dénomination sociale) may be in French or in a foreign language if written in Latin characters; any non-Latin script used in trade (e.g., Chinese or Arabic logograms) must be accompanied by a Latin-script transliteration for purposes of the RCS entry and Kbis extract; the name must not be contrary to public order or morality and must be distinguishable from existing names and trademarks protected under Article L.711-4 of the Code de la propriété intellectuelle; for a food-import SAS, the name must not mislead as to the regulated nature or origin of the goods.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Établissement de crédit (reserved to ACPR-licensed credit institutions – CMF art. L.511-5)
Assurance / Réassurance / Courtier d'assurance (reserved to ACPR-licensed insurers – Code des assurances, art. L.310-1)
Avocat / Notaire / Huissier / Expert-Comptable (reserved to regulated legal and accounting professions)
République / France / État / Ministère (national-emblem reference requiring proof that no false impression of state authority is created)
Bourse / Société de gestion / Valeurs mobilières (reserved to AMF-licensed investment firms)
Europe / Union Européenne (usable only where the entity objectively has cross-border EU activity and substance, otherwise misleading and subject to registrar rejection)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a separate pre-incorporation name-reservation system: the name is validated as part of the single registration file filed at the Guichet unique, and is factually protected only upon registration at the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS). If the INPI registrar (greffe du tribunal de commerce) refuses: (1) file supplementary observations and corrective documentation within 15 days of the notification; (2) if the defect is substantive, amend the articles of association and re-submit a new registration package via the Guichet unique within 30 days; (3) in case of refusal in fact or law, lodge an action by simple request before the President of the Tribunal de commerce (or Tribunal judiciaire where the company is non-commercial) under the final paragraph of article L.210-3 of the Code de commerce, to be brought within 15 days of notification of the refusal and ruled upon as a matter of urgency; (4) no de jure extension of the 30-day functional validation window exists – a renewed name search and a new filing cycle constitute the operational equivalent of an extension.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible with conditions for the first five years: a French SAS may register its statutory seat at an approved commercial domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) under article L.123-11-1 of the Code de commerce and article 41 of Décret n° 84-406; however, the domiciliation service must be complemented by a real operational presence or binding contracts with licensed cold-chain logistics providers in order to satisfy customs, DGAL sanitary registration and contractual substance expectations; for a meat and seafood importer, exclusive reliance on a virtual office is assessed as commercially inadequate and likely to be challenged by the French bank during Swift-TT/Revolving-LC account opening.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified composite risk: approximately 20% of import consignments of frozen beef or pelagic fish are selected by DGAL/DGCCRF for unannounced documentary and identity checks at the first Border Control Post under Regulation (EU) 2017/625; approximately 3-5% of consignments undergo physical sanitary inspection with possible sampling; the likelihood of an unannounced on-site corporate substance inspection at the registered office is approximately 5% in the first year; DGCCRF consumer-protection and traceability visits on the importer's business premises may reach 10% in the first operating year for meat-seafood importers.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: France's Code de commerce (Commercial Code), Book II, Title I and Title II; applicable provisions include Articles L.210-1 to L.210-9 (general rules), L.221-1 to L.225-101 and L.227-1 to L.227-27 (simplified joint-stock company, SAS), and Articles R.210-1 to R.227-1; supplemented by Decree No. 2023-253 on the Guichet Unique and EU Regulation 2019/941.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (commercial court registry) – application routed through the INPI Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Formulaire de création d'une société (M0) submitted electronically, together with the signed Articles of Association (Statuts) and annexes required by the registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum for SAS. The capital must be fully subscribed and divided into shares; cash contributions are deposited with a notary or a French bank in a blocked escrow account (séquestre) before registration, unless the articles elect the five-year deferral permitted by Article L.227-3 C. com.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The founding shareholders hereby adopt the Articles of Association and constitute the share capital, fully subscribed and paid up as stated therein. (2) The registered office is fixed at [Registered Address], France. (3) The shareholders appoint [Name] as President of the Société par Actions Simplifiée, vested with the broadest powers to bind the Company, open and manage bank accounts, negotiate and issue documentary credits, and complete all import formalities. (4) The President is authorized to file the incorporation application with the French Registry, publish all legal notices, and execute related documents and declarations of beneficial ownership. (5) These resolutions take effect immediately upon signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name availability and trademark pre-screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) online databases; with the legal service of the commercial court registry (Greffe).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a free search of the French national business name database and trademark register at data.inpi.fr. Ensure the proposed corporate name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered business name or trademark. Retain printed search results as evidence.
required_dossiers: Documentation of the identity of each founding shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is unavailable or opposed, select the next alternative name from the list, or contact the INPI for possible consent; no filing fee is lost at this step.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and signing of the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private draft by the legal advisor or notaire; signature before a notary is required only if an in-kind contribution includes real estate or if notarization is chosen voluntarily.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts in French with mandatory legal clauses: corporate form (SAS), corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose (including wholesale deep-frozen meat/fish import), share capital amount, share subscription and issuance rules, number of shares, rights and obligations of shareholders, terms of the Président, decision-making rules, duration (99 years max), and administrative formalities. Verify each shareholder's capacity and have all pages signed and initialed by all shareholders. Attach to the document a proxy if a shareholder is not signing in person.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe or notaire queries a clause, amend the offending provision by unanimous shareholder decision and republish the corrected statuts before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of cash share capital and publication of a legal incorporation notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any French bank, notaire, or the Caisse des Dépôts for escrow deposit; an approved legal gazette (Journal d'Annonces Légales) for the publication.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account at a French bank or with the notaire to hold the share capital. Transfer the promised cash capital and obtain an irrevocable certificate of deposit naming the future company as beneficiary. Then publish a legal notice in an approved legal gazette (JAL) within the jurisdiction of the future registered office, containing company name, legal form, capital amount, registered office address, corporate object, duration, and the identity of the President. The JAL certificate must be issued before the file submission and must be produced to the Guichet Unique.
required_dossiers: Deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication is defective or the capital certificate is missing, re-deposit or publish an amendment notice at the same gazette; the original date of deposit may be preserved if the correction is made within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of incorporation file via the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) acting as the electronic single window; files are routed to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and the URSSAF/CNI for tax and social registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the online service, select 'Créer une entreprise' under sociétés commerciales, choose SAS and the APE/NAF code corresponding to wholesale of meat and meat products (4632A or appropriate code for frozen meat/seafood import). Complete the statutory declaration (Formulaire M0), upload all required dossiers, pay the published Greffe fee, and submit. The platform will issue a proof of filing with a date of deposit. Maintain a copy of the submission receipt for follow-up.
required_dossiers: Copy of ID of President and all shareholders
Declaration of beneficial owners (formulaire liste des bénéficiaires effectifs)
Acceptance of appointment by President and auditors (if any)
Original copy of the registered office lease or deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet returns the file for incompleteness, the applicant will receive an electronic notice indicating all missing items; the file may be corrected and re-submitted within 15 days without losing the original filing date. If summarily refused, an appeal may be filed with the supervising judge of the Commercial Court within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Greffe examination, registration in the RCS, and issuance of the K-bis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (competent territorial registry) and INSEE (for SIREN/SIRET).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the dossier passes formal control, the Greffe registers the company in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS). INSEE allocates a SIREN (enterprise number) and SIRET (establishment number), and the company is automatically given an APE code corresponding to its principal activity. The Greffe then delivers an official 'Extrait K-bis' certifying legal existence and powers of legal representatives. The BODACC registration notice is published automatically.
required_dossiers: No further dossiers; this step is internal after submission
Original submission receipt may be requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed beyond the statutory deadline, the applicant may petition the Greffe in writing and, if necessary, appeal to the President of the Commercial Court with a request for interim relief (référé) to obtain a decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration fiscal, customs and employment declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP) for tax number and VAT; Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) for EORI and customs authorization; URSSAF for payroll.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receipt of the K-bis, obtain the company's SIRET number and the French value-added tax (TVA) identification number from the DGFIP (if not already completed via the Guichet Unique). Apply online to the DGDDI for an Economic Operator Registration and Identification (EORI) number to enable customs clearance for import operations. If hiring employees, within 10 days complete the URSSAF registration to contribute to social security.
required_dossiers: Copy of the registered office property
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or customs identification is delayed or rejected, file with the relevant public office, verify that the activity code (APE) is correct, and contact the corporate services of DGDDI for administrative rectification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Agriculture et de la Souveraineté Alimentaire - Direction Générale de l'Alimentation (DGAL), with local enforcement through the Direction Départementale de la Protection des Populations (DDPP) in the place of establishment.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Agrément sanitaire pour l'entreposage en froid de produits d'origine animale (sanitary approval for cold storage of food of animal origin) combined with the registered importer/trader declaration under Regulation (EC) No. 853/2004.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition écologique and Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) — service chargé des installations classées pour la protection de l'environnement (ICPE).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: ICPE Registration (Enregistrement) or Declaration under Rubrique 2220 (refrigerated warehouse) depending on refrigerant type and quantity; installations using ammonia in quantities above 150 kg require an Authorization with full EIA and public inquiry.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the ICPE Order of 3 August 2020 and EU F-gas Regulation 2024/982/EC. Refrigerant leaks must be zero; periodical leak checks are mandatory. Wastewater from cleaning operations must meet municipal sewer discharge standards (code de la santé publique art. L1331-1); condensates may be drained after a grease/oil interceptor. All organic and packaging waste must be traceable to authorized recovery or disposal routes under Regulation (EC) No. 1069/2009 and Order of 3 March 2012. Odour and noise levels must not exceed the limits set by the local arrêté préfectoral.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification by the municipal Commission de sécurité (or prefectural delegation) covering fire alarm, emergency evacuation, first-aid equipment and structural load capacity; workplace clearance by the DREETS/DDETSPP (occupational safety and health) according to the Code du travail, including mandatory safety registry, signage, and annual verification of refrigeration/electrical equipment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The European Central Bank (ECB) sets euro-area monetary policy. Banque de France is France's national central bank and performs Eurosystem and payment-system functions. The Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution (ACPR), within Banque de France, supervises French banking and insurance institutions. The French Treasury (Direction générale du Trésor) administers relevant national financial and monetary rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro and applies EU rules on free movement of capital and payments. There is no general exchange control, mandatory conversion into euros, or prior authorization for ordinary cross-border commercial payments or capital contributions. Current-account payments, dividends, and capital transactions may generally be made through regulated payment providers, subject to sanctions, AML/CFT, tax, corporate-law, bank documentation, and applicable statistical-reporting requirements. Dividend remittances require distributable profits, duly approved accounts and resolutions, and withholding-tax analysis; treaty or EU relief may require evidence of residence, beneficial ownership, and satisfaction of anti-abuse conditions. Interest, royalties, service fees, and shareholder-loan payments require substantiation, transfer-pricing support where applicable, and withholding-tax review. Banks may request source-of-funds, transaction-purpose, invoice, customs, and beneficiary information and may delay or reject transactions under their compliance controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory deadline requiring export proceeds to be repatriated and no mandatory surrender or conversion ratio for ordinary commercial export receipts. Export receipts may be retained in foreign-currency accounts, subject to bank terms, sanctions, AML/CFT controls, accounting and tax rules, and any applicable statistical-reporting obligations. The company should retain contracts, invoices, transport and customs records, and bank confirmations to substantiate receipts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for subscription funds before registration, followed by an Operational Account; subject to product availability and bank acceptance

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and relevant regional Crédit Agricole caisse
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for subscription funds before registration, followed by an Operational Account; availability and onboarding are handled by the relevant group entity
Capital Escrow Account for subscription funds before registration, followed by an Operational Account; subject to product availability and bank acceptance

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE group, including Banque Populaire and Caisse d'Epargne entities
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for subscription funds before registration, followed by an Operational Account; account relationship is with the relevant group entity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for routine euro collections and payments, subject to the provider's French or EEA authorization, permitted services, country coverage, and risk appetite. An electronic money institution is not a bank; safeguarded client funds are not necessarily covered by a deposit-guarantee scheme. Confirm legal-entity onboarding, French IBAN and payment functionality, foreign-currency availability, payment limits, direct-debit support, and access to SWIFT before reliance. An EMI should not be assumed to provide a French statutory capital-deposit certificate, revolving trade finance, documentary letters of credit, or bank credit. Do not use an offshore provider to circumvent sanctions, AML controls, or a bank's onboarding decision.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not generally require directors or shareholders to attend a bank branch in person solely to open a corporate account. Remote onboarding may be available, but each bank sets its own risk-based process and may require a live interview, certified or apostilled documents, wet-ink signatures, or in-person verification. Non-resident ownership is permitted for a SAS, but non-resident directors, complex ownership chains, high-risk jurisdictions, and non-French source-of-funds may lead to enhanced due diligence or a physical meeting. For a company in formation, obtain the bank's capital-deposit process and required incorporation documents before collecting subscriptions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership, nominee arrangements, layered holding companies, or inability to identify natural-person beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current group organization chart to natural-person level; registers and constitutional documents for each ownership layer; shareholder and director registers; identification and proof of address for beneficial owners and authorized signatories; French beneficial-ownership filing evidence when applicable; explanations and supporting documents for any nominee or trust arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital or working-capital funding from an unrelated party, a high-risk jurisdiction, or an account not held in the contributor's name
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription, shareholder-loan, or financing documents; board or shareholder approvals; bank statements showing the funding trail; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; contributor ownership and identity documents; clear payment reference identifying the legal basis and recipient SAS.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business profile inconsistent with a frozen beef and seafood wholesaler, including unexplained third-party payments, cash activity, or mismatched counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan and product list; supplier and customer contracts; invoices and purchase orders; expected transaction volumes and currencies; shipping and cold-chain documents; customs declarations; food-business and sanitary approvals where required; payment-flow chart identifying payer, payee, country, and commercial purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering indicators, including unusual price, quantity, routing, transshipment, vessel, or goods-description discrepancies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Purchase and sale contracts; commercial invoices; packing lists; bills of lading or equivalent transport documents; insurance documents; customs and import records; certificates of origin and sanitary certificates as applicable; independent price support; explanation of intermediaries and routing; reconciliation of goods, invoices, and payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, restricted-party, or elevated-country exposure involving suppliers, customers, beneficial owners, vessels, banks, or transit routes
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documented screening of counterparties, beneficial owners, vessels, banks, and relevant jurisdictions against applicable EU, UN, and French sanctions measures; transaction-specific screening logs; ownership and control analysis; licenses or authorizations where legally available; documented escalation and rejection procedures. Screening does not replace legal sanctions analysis.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained payment-purpose information, frequent third-party settlement, or divergence between invoices, customs records, and bank transfers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Invoice-to-payment reconciliation; contractual payment terms; explanation of agents, factors, or group treasury entities; mandates and agency agreements; commercial rationale for third-party payments; transaction references and supporting shipping or customs records; written internal approval trail.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route subscriptions and shareholder funding from an account in the contributor's own name to the designated French bank capital-deposit account or, after registration, the SAS's operational account. Identify the payment as share capital, share premium, or shareholder loan and include the subscriber or lender name, SAS name, and supporting reference. Supply the bank with subscription documents, incorporation evidence, ownership information, source-of-funds evidence, and any requested tax-residence or regulatory forms. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments where available and SWIFT for other currencies or non-SEPA origins. Do not rely on a universal French bank purpose-code system; provide a precise narrative and transaction documents. Reconcile receipt to corporate records and obtain the capital-deposit certificate where required for formation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro-denominated EEA payments where supported, and SWIFT customer credit transfers (commonly documented as MT103 or its ISO 20022 equivalent) for other cross-border payments. Match beneficiary name, account, bank identifiers, currency, invoice number, contract, shipment, and payment terms. For supplier risk mitigation, request a documentary commercial letter of credit issued or confirmed by a bank, subject to credit approval, collateral, and applicable ICC rules such as UCP 600 where incorporated. Documentary collections may be considered where appropriate. Retain invoices, purchase orders, transport and customs documents, sanctions-screening evidence, and payment confirmations. Agree allocation of charges and FX conversion terms in advance; reconcile bank fees and short payments. Payments remain subject to bank screening and applicable EU sanctions and AML/CFT requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards to hedge documented or otherwise supportable foreign-currency trade exposures, subject to bank onboarding, credit limits, suitability and appropriateness requirements where applicable, and execution documentation.

Non-deliverable forwards where offered for a currency with restricted convertibility or settlement, subject to counterparty acceptance, product classification, and applicable EU financial-markets rules.

Currency swaps or cross-currency swaps to manage documented funding or cash-flow exposures, subject to credit approval, collateral and netting documentation, and applicable EMIR reporting, risk-mitigation, and clearing requirements.

Spot foreign-exchange transactions for near-term settlement of supplier or customer payments; maintain an exposure register, authorized dealing limits, documented counterparty confirmations, and periodic hedge-effectiveness and accounting reviews.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and allocation of profit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end; minutes and resolutions must be retained at the registered office.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Potential director liability, court-ordered compliance, and penalties for failure to file approved accounts; no automatic strike-off on a fixed statutory date.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual accounts, management report where applicable, and auditor report where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial court registry through the French one-stop business formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval of the accounts, or within two months if filed electronically.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction and civil fine may apply; repeated or prolonged non-compliance may lead to administrative removal from the Commercial and Companies Register after formal notice, with no universal fixed strike-off period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return, Form 2065 and supporting schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally by the second business day after 1 May following the relevant financial year-end; for financial years not ending on 31 December, generally within three months after year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing interest generally accrues at 0.20% per month, with a 10% surcharge that may increase for non-compliance or formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate register and beneficial ownership review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records; modifications to beneficial ownership information are filed with the French business formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Review at least annually; beneficial ownership changes must generally be reported within 30 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update beneficial ownership information may result in criminal penalties, court injunctions, and restrictions or removal measures affecting the company registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SAS generally must appoint a statutory auditor when it exceeds at least two of the following thresholds at financial year-end: EUR 5 million total balance sheet assets, EUR 10 million turnover excluding tax, and 50 employees. Appointment may also be required for certain controlled or controlling groups, or ordered following a qualifying shareholder request.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the French Accounting Standards Authority regulations; IFRS may be used in limited circumstances but is not the default statutory framework for an SAS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require a separate annual beneficial ownership confirmation solely because a new year begins. The company must review ownership and control information annually and file any change generally within 30 days. Share transfers must be recorded in the relevant securities account and transfer documentation, with corresponding updates to corporate records.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register or record of shareholder securities accounts and share transfers
Register of shareholders or equivalent shareholder ownership records
Register of corporate decisions and minutes
Beneficial ownership records and filed declarations
Records of directors and corporate officers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 650-1,950 per year, depending on location and whether mail handling, domiciliation, or corporate secretarial services are included.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 3,000-10,000 per year for a small SAS subject to statutory audit; USD 0 where no statutory auditor is required.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for the first EUR 38,120 of taxable profit for SME companies satisfying Article 44 sexies-0 CGI conditions; research tax credit (CIR) at 30% on R&D expenses up to EUR 100M per year and 5% thereafter; innovation tax credit (CII); young innovative enterprise (JEI) partial exemptions; no sector-specific tax holiday for frozen meat/seafood wholesalers under ISIC 4632.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (per Article 209 CGI forward carry is indefinite, but annual offset is capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable income above EUR 1,000,000; a 1-year carryback option capped at EUR 1,000,000 also exists).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (liasse fiscale) via professional e-filing portal at impots.gouv.fr; EFI/EDI mandatory for SAS under Article 1649 quinquies B bis CGI; IRDM module for integrated data entry.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual CIT return plus four quarterly instalment payments in March, June, September and December, with the balance due by the statutory filing deadline.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a 31 December fiscal year-end: file by the second business day after 1 May. For other fiscal year-ends: file no later than the third business day following the expiry of three months after the closing date. E-filing extensions apply automatically.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification, SIREN, APE/NAF code 4632Z, legal form SAS, registered office, fiscal year opening and closing dates, and place of tax residence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A French SAS, even if wholly foreign-owned, files as a French resident entity and must enter its French registered address. Non-resident shareholders do not file this form; the SAS itself is the taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fixed and current assets, equity, provisions, liabilities, intra-group receivables and payables, and off-balance-sheet commitments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all assets and liabilities held by the French SAS, including cold-chain storage assets and inventories of imported frozen beef and pelagic fish. Foreign-currency receivables are converted into EUR at the year-end closing rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue, other operating income, purchases of frozen meat/seafood, cold storage and logistics costs, personnel costs, depreciation, financial income and expense, and net taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognise import purchase costs at arm's length and record intercompany expenses under transfer pricing rules. Freight and customs duties are capitalisable under French GAAP only where mandatory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net income, reconciliation of non-deductible expenses under Article 39 CGI, tax result, carried-forward deficits, corporate income tax calculation, and CVAE/CFE data.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the French tax result after applying Article 209 deficit carryforward rules. No DTA deduction is claimed on the return itself; any foreign tax credit for the benefit of the French SAS is recorded separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of controlled intercompany transactions, loans, royalties, cost-sharing arrangements, and any advance pricing agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Required when the French SAS meets the EUR 400M turnover or total asset threshold, or when its foreign group has more than EUR 750M consolidated revenue. Attach Master File and Local File under Article L.13 AA/AB LPF.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business value added declaration used for the territorial economic contribution, based on turnover and value added.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the French SAS has annual turnover above EUR 152,000 on French wholesale sales, it must file the CVAE declaration. Treaty relief does not apply to this local levy.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: No daily surcharge for CIT; late payment interest accrues at 0.20% per month. Late filing after formal notice attracts a 10% majoration under Article 1728 CGI; deliberate concealment carries 40%; fraudulent declarations or abuse of law carry 80%. Failure to file a nil return triggers a minimum EUR 150 penalty. Additional penalties may be imposed for missing transfer pricing documentation and for non-cooperation with an audit.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% for non-resident corporate shareholders under Article 119 bis CGI; 12.8% for non-resident individuals plus applicable social levies where France has taxing rights. Treaty rates may reduce the domestic rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced DTA rate, obtain a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) in the shareholder's home jurisdiction and submit to the French paying agent before dividend distribution using form 5000. If withholding is applied at the statutory 25%, file a reclaim with the Direction des grandes entreprises or the local tax office within five years, attaching the TRC, holding-period evidence, and a beneficial ownership declaration.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic royalty withholding tax under Article 182 B CGI is 33.33% of the gross amount unless a treaty overrides it; most French DTAs cap industrial royalties at 5% and copyright royalties at 0%. Interest paid to non-resident corporate lenders is generally exempt from domestic withholding tax on ordinary bank or private debt, but certain profit-sharing or convertible bonds may incur 30%; most French DTAs reduce interest withholding to 0%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 annual turnover or total assets in France triggers mandatory Master File and Local File documentation under Article L.13 AA/AB LPF. EUR 750,000,000 consolidated group revenue triggers French Country-by-Country Reporting under Article 223 quinquies C CGI.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply a separate Economic Substances Regulations code, but the substance-over-form doctrine and anti-abuse rules require genuine commercial substance for any French SAS or permanent establishment. The French entity must demonstrate local management, operational staff, cold-chain infrastructure, meaningful purchasing and logistics activities, and assumption of commercial risk. Absent substance, tax authorities invoke Article L.64 LPF, Article 57 CGI, and treaty restriction under the BEPS MLI principal purpose test.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting imported frozen meat or seafood sales, issuing fictitious invoices, falsifying cold-chain inventory records, or concealing bank receipts from Swiss or other foreign accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 80% tax penalty under Article 1729 CGI plus late-payment interest; criminal prosecution under Article 1741 CGI with a fine up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment for five years, increased to EUR 1,000,000 and seven years for organised or aggravated fraud. The tax administration may recover the full concealed tax base and social security contributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who participated in preparing false declarations are jointly liable for the company's tax debt and penalties under Article L.267 LPF. Conviction can lead to travel bans, asset seizure, commercial disqualification, and imprisonment. Civil restitution orders may attach personal wealth if the corporate veil is pierced.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company or abuse of law
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Interposing the French SAS or an offshore parent as a non-substantive mailbox company to divert licensing income, capital gains, or dividends from the true economic owner and thus avoid French withholding tax or corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Abuse of law under Article L.64 LPF triggers an 80% penalty, reassessment at the level of the real beneficial owner, and denial of treaty benefits under the principal purpose test. The transaction is recharacterised, and additional withholding tax becomes immediately payable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the artificial entity may be jointly liable for reassessed taxes and penalties under Article L.267 LPF. If they caused or knew of the sham, they may also face criminal sanctions, personal civil damages, travel restrictions, and confiscation orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting non-arm's-length purchase prices for frozen beef or seafood bought from related suppliers, paying excessive royalty or storage fees to related entities, or providing no reward for the French SAS's cold-chain logistics functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment under Article 57 CGI to real arm's-length price, plus penalties: 40% for deliberate mispricing and up to 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres. Failure to provide transfer pricing documentation within 30 days of request incurs a fine up to EUR 150,000 or 5% of the reassessed result, whichever is higher, under Article 1735 bis CGI.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who designed or approved artificial transfer prices can be personally held liable for the resulting tax deficiencies under Article L.267 LPF. Egregious conduct may trigger criminal tax fraud prosecution, professional bans, and seizure of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using Revolving LC and Swift TT payment rails to conceal beneficial ownership, move proceeds through shell trade companies, or evade customs duties on imported frozen carcasses and pelagic fish, including deliberate failure to report suspicious transactions to TRACFIN.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering under Article 324-1 of the French Criminal Code is punishable by up to five years imprisonment and a EUR 375,000 fine for natural persons; aggravated or organised laundering carries ten years and EUR 750,000. Customs fraud penalties may add one to three times the evaded duties. Administrative sanctions from ACPR and TRACFIN may include licence withdrawal and financial fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who structured or knowingly tolerated money laundering risk personal prosecution, travel bans, asset confiscation, and disqualification from French corporate management. Civil restitution can attach personal assets, and the corporate veil is pierced for deliberate AML non-compliance.
